title: Suspected bacterial meningitis at 48 with alcohol use disorder, on vancomycin and ceftriaxone without ampicillin

provenance.author: Claude Code (draft for owner review), converted from an ambiguous case on the owner's correction

clinical_review.notes: Owner clinical review: revised text approved after conversion to a negative control.

story: A 48-year-old man with alcohol use disorder presents with fever, headache and neck stiffness; CSF shows a neutrophilic pleocytosis with low glucose. Empiric vancomycin, ceftriaxone and dexamethasone are started; cultures are pending. Ampicillin is not ordered; he is not immunocompromised.

reference_answer: No intervention. Vancomycin plus a third-generation cephalosporin with dexamethasone is the empiric regimen for an adult under 50 who is not immunocompromised; alcohol use disorder is not an indication for empiric ampicillin. Narrow therapy when cultures return.
rationale: A negative control at the age boundary: under 50, not immunocompromised, with alcohol use disorder. Alcohol use disorder is not a risk factor that calls for Listeria coverage (owner's clinical review, 2026-10-25). A rule that adds ampicillin for comorbidities other than age and immunocompromise fails this case.
